note: Review-only file, not for insertion into TestsData. Correct-option rationales included; technical/distractor editorial check remains recommended.

questions.text: A user enters example.com and receives the matching IP address before connecting to the site. Which service most directly performs this name resolution?
questions.rationale: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses.

questions.text: A page loads HTML successfully, but a separately linked style file cannot be fetched. Which request/result is most relevant to investigate?

options.label: D
options.text: The stylesheet URL and server response for the CSS resource

questions.rationale: A failed external stylesheet request prevents those styles from loading.

questions.text: A form submits login details over an unencrypted HTTP connection. What is the primary risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Credentials may be exposed in transit

options.label: C
options.text: DNS converts the password into a domain

options.label: D
options.text: The CSS box model stops working

questions.rationale: HTTP alone does not encrypt content in transit.

questions.text: A browser sends web requests, but the app needs reliable, ordered delivery for the data. Which transport is typically appropriate?
questions.rationale: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream.

questions.text: A real-time service prefers low overhead and can tolerate some packet loss without waiting for retransmission. Which transport may fit?
questions.rationale: UDP avoids TCP's connection and retransmission mechanisms.

questions.text: A user needs to transfer a file to a server using the protocol named in the syllabus. Which choice fits?
questions.rationale: FTP is designed for file transfer.

questions.text: A developer serves the same HTML document over HTTP and HTTPS. What does the HTTPS version add when configured correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: Guaranteed correctness of every page statement

options.label: C
options.text: TLS protection for data exchanged between client and server

questions.rationale: HTTPS uses TLS to protect the connection, not to validate content accuracy.

questions.text: A site owner changes a domain's DNS record but some users still reach the old server temporarily. Which explanation is plausible?

options.label: A
options.text: Cached DNS data may persist until its TTL or cache expires

questions.rationale: Resolvers and clients may cache DNS answers.

questions.text: A site is accessible from a network but not by entering its domain, while a known IP address works. Which issue is worth checking first?
questions.rationale: Success by IP but failure by domain points toward name resolution.

questions.text: A website uses a numeric IPv4 address and a newer 128-bit IPv6 address. Which statement is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: IPv6 is a CSS stylesheet type

options.label: C
options.text: IPv4 uses 128 bits and IPv6 uses 32

options.label: D
options.text: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses
